sentences.text: This meeting is being recorded.
Hello.
Hi, Manu.
Hey Andy.
Good, thanks mate.
How are you?
I'm good, I'm good.
Whereabouts are you based then?
I'm in Sydney.
In Sydney.
Ah, fantastic.
Cool.
Thanks for jumping on.
Late for me.
Yeah, late for you, early for me.
I was living in LA year before last for six months.
I don't know what it's like in Sydney but the culture there is.
Everybody gets up at sort of five in the morning and goes to the gym.
Okay.
Is it 5am for you?
Sorry, is it flyer for you?
Nope, it's 805.
Okay, cool.
But I'm just, I'm back in the UK and that culture is on the other side of the planet.
So what's it like in Sydney?
Early.
Early mornings?
No, not really.
We're pretty chill.
Yeah, we're pretty chill.
Like we'll start like 9am usually.
Just your regular nine to fives every.
Once in a generation.
Unless you're doing like investment banking or something.
Yeah, no, it's everybody in la, but yeah, it's good to know that Australians are sticking to the character that they're well known for.
Yeah, that's right.
So.
Well, thank you for replying to my emails.
I think there's a couple of times actually where you've said you're, you're interested in doing a roll up, so.
Yeah, I'm not, I'm not really sure to be honest.
I just thought it sounds like, you know what might be.
Yeah, have some recommendations.
So I thought I'd just, yeah, be helpful to jump on either way.
Yeah, cool.
All right, well let me tell you a little bit about me.

I know you probably get my emails, but in terms of, of what we do, so we are an M and A advisory called Capital A Group and we have a couple of platforms that we work from because we work both on the buy and the sell side.
So our sell side platform is Agencies Co where we work with agency owners helping them to exit.
And on the buy side we, we have the M and A advisory, Capital A and also Deal Engines, which is like a deal flow tool platform as well.
So we get to see a lot of deals but both on the buy and sell side, you know, making offers ourselves as well as accepting them or negotiating them from potential buyers.

So on this occasion we've started building our own roll up as well as an option to founders just because what we see in the market is there's a lot of investment bankers like you said, who get up at 5, maybe deservedly so in some instances.
But what they do is they take some of the, the value that's created by forming a larger company for themselves and what we're hoping to do is give some of that back to founders.
So instead of getting a five or maybe a six times multiple for a certain size business, they could only get in an eight or nine times multiple and we would hand back that gap to them.
So they could almost double what they're getting for their business.
But it'd be good to, to find out a little bit more about you and Nuva Digital.
So you're in Sydney.
Tell me how you got Neva started.
Is that your business or are you.
Yeah, it's my business.
Yeah.
I'm the only founder, I'm the only employee actually.
Everything it's kind of right now is mostly well I have like full time employees but on, on the books technically they're subcontracting.
Right.
But they work full time with me.
Um, and yeah it's been like five years now been running and we work with E commerce brands so solely mostly e commerce brands.
A few other clients here or there but it's now fully E commerce.
When we started it was like all sorts of clients but I narrowed it down to E commerce.

The Australian market is obviously there's, there's a lot of agencies so there's, there is that but I feel like there's not a lot of highly experienced agencies with like you know, people with my sort of skill level that are, that are running them.

So yeah, it's kind of, that's kind of how I've created that niche for myself where I, I bring in, I try to learn about from the Australian, the US processes and what the big guys are doing in the US and bring that to Australia.
So that gives us a pretty unique proposition.
So we kind of do full service E commerce the focus of the core.
And it started off with advertising like paid ads across Facebook, Instagram and TikTok.

But now it's kind of become content production, video editing, graphic design, Shopify development, you know, landing pages conversion, rate optimization, just email marketing, just everything that an E commerce brand would need.
And we kind of roll that into one retainer and then have our team deliver.
So yeah, that's kind of the rundown.
Of what we do.
So your freelance team, how many people do you have so regularly working as if they were permanences?
About 15.
That's quite big team.
Do you mind giving me some, some numbers?
Just, they can just be sort of ballpark but in terms of like revenue, what Are you roughly doing.
Yeah.
So revenue is about 100k Australian per month, and that's generally around a.
A gross profit of around 50%.
And what's your net profit?
Do you know?
Net profit as in after tax?
Well, yeah, I mean it can be, but EBITDA is what I'm shooting for, really, because that's the number we work for.
That should be.
That's, that's the profit that I just gave you, I think after expenses and.
It'S 50% and then you tax on that and you've got your net.
Okay.
Yeah.
Okay.
Yeah.
So that's like all expenses, all the staff wages.
I see you're allocating to direct, direct cost here.
And then everything left is yours anyway, even though that's the gross profit.
Right, I got you.
Yeah.
Okay, so 50, right.
What's that in dollars or pounds?
Let's figure out where you are.
So Australian $1 to 1 pound to $2 is.
Okay, so about 50,000 pounds a month, which is great.
Yeah.
The Australian economy is a little bit down at the moment.
If this was a year ago, it would have looked better.
Oh yeah, the exchange rates are.
Well, it's a nightmare right now, isn't it?
Yeah.
Not usual.
Okay.
And then.
So what you thinking?
Tell me what your, your goals are in terms of what you're trying to achieve.
Five years is obviously a really established, you know, period of time to get an agency up and running.
Yeah.
So what's your goals right now?
And yeah, so it's taken this time to kind of really figure out what is the offer, what is the target market, what are we delivering and build all the process around that.
But now I'm in a position where I've done that.
I know exactly what our offer is.
I know like what our pricing is.
I know how we kind of grow with our clients.
I know how to deliver the.
A lot of it is documented.
And what I envision the next step would be is kind of to franchise the agency.

Not franchise, but it's kind of like you have someone like me who comes in and they manage a book of clients and so they close the deal and they manage the client and they deliver the service with the client and they manage the team end to end.
And you could have like 10 of me's who are using my process and then they're using my lead generation, which, which I have a system for as well, and all my experience.
And then they're basically servicing these clients.
And then that would be how I would scale and build out the agency.
Rather than like we bring in an employee that manages this service and we bring one that manages this service.
The way that I've done it is one person leads the entire strategy for the client and they do the sales and they work with the client.
And that leads to really strong client retention because they're always working with that one person that is the one that brought them into the agency and that's the only person that they talk to.
And that person then manages the team and delivers everything for the client.
So that's kind of the way that I see the agency growing.
For me though, personally, I'm kind of like, I don't know if I want to be the one that goes ahead and builds that out and does that on my own.
I kind of did it this year.
So over the last year I've brought someone on and I've done this exact model with him where I'm like, cool, here's everything I do.
And I've taken him from basically zero, where he doesn't even know like you know, how to run ads, to closing a deal and managing clients end to end.
And now he's managing like his own book of clients and kind of.
And that's there some training scheme.
And how long did that take you to, to train them up?
It took a year.
It took a full year.
I mean what's the process?
Are they, they ghosting you or are you satisfied?
Like almost in a classroom and.
Yeah, they basically.
That's right, they ghost me for three months straight looking at exactly what I do and then they start to manage a few processes for the clients.
So they take on, let me just take on this service.
Let me take on this service.
This service.

They're watching me end to end and then they join me on sales calls and they look at how I run my sales process, how I close deals, how I screen share and you know, it's a very solution based selling.
There's no scams, there's no like give me a deposit.
It's very like, it's just straight, you know, just straight business practice.
Like, hey, this is what we can do.
I think we can help you or I don't think we can help you.
And then yeah, so like over the last two months he's closed, you know, three of his own deals.
He's managing those clients end to end.
And yeah, and he's super young, like he's only 23.
So if someone came in with experience, the process would have been a lot faster.
Yeah, but yeah, we have some really strong case Studies in the Australian market.
Like, we've worked with the, the one of the Shark Tank Australia judges who's like the most well known person in E commerce in Australia.
And we have a reputation with him.
Yeah.
What are you doing with.
I can't remember his name now.
He's called Davey Fogarty.
David Fogarty.
And what are you doing with him?
So we worked with him, two of his legacy brands, we helped him sell out that stock and then he actually referred us all the Shark Tank deals after that.
So all the deals that he did on the show, they came to us and we managed their ads and stuff like that.
And we're still working with some of those, some of those brands.
So those kind of case studies under the belt, plus we've taken multiple brands from zero to a million per month.
Um, so I kind of leverage those case studies to do the lead generation and run our own ads.
Um, and then.
Yeah, but it's kind of like I'm, I'm personally always at capacity.
This is the first time where I've brought someone on who has capacity who can then take on clients.
But yeah, I mean, it wasn't easy.
And so I'm kind of like, yeah, I don't know, I'm interested to see, like, is this something that someone sees of value and.
Yeah.
Is there an exit plan for me and, and what's kind of the scope?
Yeah, so.
So, yeah, sure.
I mean, it really does depend on, on what kind of exit you're looking for yourself personally.
And also a lot that's associated with that is, is the number, you know, the magic number that you want to go out for.
So very generally speaking, agencies go somewhere in the region of four to six.
Typically it's not set in stone at all.

And there's lots of variables associated with that, but certainly that would kind of be at least a, a starting point somewhere around a 4x, particularly for a business of your size, which is less than sort of a million dollars in revenues, that would be sort of the 3, 4, 5 mark, and that's EBITDAR.
So if your Eidar is about what we're looking at, 600,000 Australian a year, then then you're probably looking at, you know, 2.4 million maybe in terms of the, the valuation that you could get.
And then that's very dependent as well on whether you want to stay in the business and how long, how long you want to stay in the business for.
You know, if you're looking to exit quickly, then it might be a smaller amount of Money.
But if you're looking to stay in the business for three years, then certainly you could expect to get the top end of, of that range.
So, yeah, that's the first thing.
And then the, this, the, the other thing really is, is your timeline and what you're looking to do, what you're looking to achieve in terms of, of the exit.

You know, are you looking to, to sell soon and, and move into a large business or is, is your hope to find somebody that really likes your model and sell to that person so they can continue training people in your boot camp to take parts of the business?
Yeah, I mean, I, I'd say like, if there was a bigger company that liked the model and was like, hey, build it out for us, we'll take what you've got.
We love the service that you're offering.
We like that you've got this process and we think it's super unique.
Come in and train five of our guys.
They invest, they pay the team.
I just come in, I train these people.
I showed them how to get clients, I showed them how to close deals.
I showed them how to do that over like a year and then they can run it from there, train the next people.
You know, I would be, I think that would be the most efficient process for the business.
Rather than one person comes in, replaces me, then starts juggling my clients and then tries to hire at the same time and train at the same time.
Like, I feel like that would be, they kind of be in my position.
I feel like if a big company came in, maybe they're like, maybe they're a US Company that wants to expand into Australia or there's some, you know, they're in Singapore or something like that.
You know, they're like in another region, but they want to hit the Australian market or they're in Australia or they just, they don't care what, where the person is.
They just want to.
Yeah.
You know, build a strong consulting brand or something.
Yeah.
So we, I mean, we would, we would have to see on a case by case basis with the buyers whether that was their interest.
Most agency owners that are buying other businesses, well, they kind of fall in two categories.
One, one for this size business.
One would be an owner operator who maybe has moved to Australia or just had worked for a larger agency and wanted to set up their own agency.
And maybe they just, they had, they had some money that they wanted to invest.
And so rather than start from scratch, they would acquire a business like yours and just run it themselves.
In which case your Idea to get out quite quickly is usually quite straightforward because they just want to carry the business, the business themselves and do all the work.
Yeah, so that would work for them, particularly if you could train them in three months.
That'd be perfect.
Absolutely.
Yeah.
I'm open to staying, like I don't need to run away, you know.
Yeah.
The other type of buy would be the larger agency, in which case they're not that concerned about what you're doing right now.
They're looking at your clients and maybe your team.
They would be looking to expand, you know, quickly and so they bolt on businesses maybe like one or two a year so they can grow inorganically.
So the way to do that.
And again, I don't really know what your timeline is but, but we have agencies co as our platform.
We have 20,000 agency buyers on our mailing list and then we have our own database as well as 130,000 agencies globally.
They're mostly US and UK and Australia and New Zealand.
So that's kind of like that.
And Canada, those are the markets that we tend to focus on just because we can speak English really more than anything.
Yeah, of course, a little bit in Europe and the Middle east as well.
So you can list with us.
We've got a couple of sort of tiers to, to do that process.
So depending on, on what your timeline is again, is would kind of sort of influence how you want to do that.

So a lot of sellers that come with us, they want to sell and so they're happy to sort of pay the sort of larger listing fees because we work them full time on the deal and we get the deal over the line and that usually happens within a six month period.
If it's kind of more a casual affair like your thinking, then we just help you get set up, you know, work out what your valuation of the business would be.
And we build what's called an im, which is like a marketing document, like a sales deck and get you listed and get you out to our database, 20 buyers.
So what sounds more interesting to you is are you more kind of a suck it and see at the moment or is this something you're thinking you want to get done before the end of the year?
Well, I'd like to know what it looks like to do both options.
Yeah, so, well, just in terms of fees.
So we always take 5% on the deal and the 5% we take is then netted from any fees or retainers that you pay.
So just to get you up on the platform is two and A half thousand dollars.
But like I say, for that we'll do a full valuation of the business and create the IM for you.
Now we need both of those things to list, but like I say, once we've sold the business, so say we were to get, I don't know, $30,000 as our win fee.
That would be net of those two and a half thousand that you paid already.
The same with all the others.
If you were to do the full sales setup, the full process, then that's $15,000.
But like I say, we work full time for pretty much six months to get the business sold.
Sometimes a little quicker than that, sometimes it's a bit longer.
Right, Okay.
I can put both of those options in a, an email Monday if it's not something that'll be good now.
But I mean, what, what is your timeline?
What are you trying to achieve?
Look, I, I'm not in a rush.
I think, I don't think I'm in a rush.
Yeah, I definitely want to get the best out of it that I can.
Now.
Or is, or is it something that you, you're thinking, you know, maybe next month, maybe the.
Maybe.
No, I think I want to go ahead and like start the process in some way.
Okay, cool.
All right.
So yeah, I mean it's good to know because otherwise, you know, I can give you the best advice on what you should be shooting for.
So let me get.
What about, what about the roll up or do you think that's not relevant here?
It's probably not an option.
So it's certainly not an option for you to be part of our roll up or most.
Sorry.
Right.
Let me say first our option.
We are looking for 1 million EBITDA businesses.
So you're too small for what we're looking for.
The reason is there is economics of scale and what's called multiple arbitrage.
And when we get to around 5 to 8 million in EBITDA with the rolled up businesses, the economics change from being sort of 7, 8, 9 to up to 10 or more.
So we're really looking to achieve that.
And the agencies we need need to be a certain size.
So for us, maybe if you get enough Australian companies, then we'll hit the 1 million in Australian dollars.
Yeah, maybe, maybe.
Well, I think that what you were thinking at first is probably more on the money.
Is it likely to be a global business that's trying to get into Australian market as well?

So yeah, okay, but, but in, in terms of where your, you know, exit could work, you could be part of A roll up, but it just wouldn't be, it wouldn't be our one and we wouldn't be specifically targeting roll ups necessarily.
A roll up usually implies that there is a time limit to get the business together so that you can sell it on.

But most agency groups, they start from one agency founder and they buy a business, they buy another business and rather than sort of call it a roll up, they're just looking to, to grow the business because they're not thinking of, of selling necessarily.
They're just building an agency group.
Okay.
So it could be that you end up being part of a roll up.
It just wouldn't be one way.
You were what we call a platform business where you start the business with one cornerstone.
It's just a size thing basically.
If maybe you're about four times bigger then that would work.
So, so I think the, the seller option is probably the main way for you to go with us.
Like I say, it's two and a half thousand US dollars and we would work with you to get you up and ready to sell, get you listed on our site.
We actually sold an Aussie guys agency last year but he's, he was in, in la.
I think I know that one.
Well, that's Spotlight.
It is Spotlight.
He's an Aussie.
Do you know him?
Everybody knows him.
It's so funny.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
It's a small market, I'm telling you here.
Yeah, that's brilliant.
Yeah.
How did, how did that work?
If you don't mind quickly just sharing.
What do you mean how did it work in terms of the deal?
I can't discuss how the deal, but we sold them to a company called Mason, Mason Interact, which are based in Chicago.
So Arjun actually was part of an Australian group of, of agencies.
They were looking to expand to the U.S.
and he took the business to the U.S.
but the parent group I think either sold or just lost interest in America.
So I took the business on, on his own and built the team.
But, but Arjun is a beautiful man.
I love him so much.
He's such a good guy.
I don't know if you know him personally but he's, he's an amazing guy.
Got a real sort of radiator personality.
So he's a good guy to, to invest in but he's not the guy that's going to run a business and grow it because he just is, he is argent.
But we found a buyer for the business and he's blossomed underneath this leadership at Mason.
So he's been there over a year now and he's due the rest of his payout, which is great.
So, yeah, I can't really talk about the details of the business but.
But yeah, I think that's, that's kind of all I wanted to know.
So everybody knows our margin and yeah, he's an AUSSIE in, in LA, which is great.
So we got 45 signed NDAs for his business in 24 hours and that's really the key.
What does that you mean like 45 people were interested?
They signed the contract to say they want more details, so they signed the privacy contract and then we're able to share the, the IM with them, which we'd build for Arjun.

So in terms of the process, this is what I'm saying, it's quite low investment from you, but once we've got you up and listed on the site and it goes out to our audience, then we can get very quick results.
And so from those 45, five went on to make offers and Arjun just picked the best one that suited him.
So it was a very quick process.
It was actually around six months, the, the entire process.
Even though Arjun only went for the, the lowest package with us, so it was a very small investment from him, just time and a, a very small payment.
So.
Yeah.
And so then it was his agreement that he would work with them for a year to get the.
He wants to stay there.
Yeah, I mean, he's not looking to get out.
He loves working at Mason, so he's a key part of their team now and he's, you know, he's a great sales guy and, and so he's.
Yeah, he's grown within the business.
He has a business within the business.
So it's a really good opportunity for Arjun.
He loves it.
He's on the west coast, but the parent business is on the east coast.
So he's jetting across America backwards and forwards, which he seems to be enjoying, which is great.
So, yeah, we would be looking to achieve something like that for you.
So if we can get you listed very quickly, now is kind of the, the best time.
I'm actually going to start sending out some emails talking about why this month and next month are the best window to, to start the process to sell your business.

Because if we can get it up and running now, the likelihood is it will sell before the end of the year and actually there's kind of a rush to, particularly with the Americans, to get bit deals closed in mid November.
And do they often acquire agencies in somewhere like Australia does that everywhere?
Yeah, American businesses And British and European will.
I think what I would say is we wouldn't close any options off.
We would look to market the entire marketplace.
We want to find the right buyer.
But yes, you're right.
There is a lot of American companies.
They just want to expand everywhere.
And if they can add an Australian agency, although once they realize they've got to get up at a certain time to speak to every day, it depends where they're based as well, I guess.
But yeah, they just want to expand everywhere.

I mean, what I would say is 99% of the work, and that's not really an exaggeration that we do, is with American companies, even if we have a British client, in fact, we had an Israeli client and we sold that business to an American company.
So.
So whether you're based in Australia or the UK or the Middle east, the likelihood is the buyer is going to be an American company.
So, yeah, there's a lot of interest.
Okay.
So what I suggest is I'll get this, the seller package in an email to you so that you've got the details and if you are happy and moving forward.
And I would, you know, given what you said and given the sort of low barrier to entry at 2 1/2 K, I would say let's get this set up because as I was saying, it's a great window before Thanksgiving.
Buyers will basically rush to get a deal done in November because they just want to take time off.
And Americans are even worse than anyone else.
They basically down tools at the end of November and they don't pick them up until mid January.
So.
So it's a good window to get started on the process.
Sure.
And you think there's like good scope based on what I've, what I've told you about the business?
Yeah, I mean, it's a, it's a perfect size.
I mean, Arjun's business in particular was, was tiny.
It was much smaller than yours, I think probably, you know, half or, or less.
Okay.
You know, he'd been struggling on his own, but we had much interest in that.
Okay.
Part, partly, I think was because it was, was in la, but the other part of it was the services that he's providing.
It's just a kind of cool space to be in and I think can be said of what you're doing.
I know you're doing kind of like a full service thing to some degree, but you're a growth marketing business and every kind of growing agency wants what you, you can do.
And quite often it's kind of the sort of.
I'm not blowing smoke up your ass, but like cool founders like yourself who, who are able to do this type of agency work, you know, it's, It's.
It's usually sort of a single founder that builds these types of businesses and the larger agencies, they just can't hire the talent to do it.
Yeah, they would much rather bolt it on, you know, if.
If they don't know how to do it in particular, but sort of the growth.
And did.
Did Arjun hit the four to six mark that you were saying?
Like, he was in that he got.
A little bit more probably.
He got an amazing deal and he's also got an earn out.
But yeah, we were, we were able to negotiate a great deal for Arjun.
The key thing was he had so many signed NDAs and we had so many offers that we could just, you know, set them off against each other and compete for a good offer.
We, we already knew who we wanted to go with because he, he very much got on with Brook, the founder of Mason from.
But we were able to push that deal because Mason knew that there was other competing interests, so they just wanted to get the deal done.
So, yeah, he got a.
A really good deal.
Okay, awesome.
Cool.
All right, let me get it sent over to you and, and hopefully we'll get the.
Well, the next step would be to get an engagement letter signed and then we can start the ball rolling.
Awesome.
Set up on the system.
Great.
Thank you so much.
I really appreciate your time.
All right, Manu, nice to speak to you too.
Enjoy the rest of your evening.
Me too.
Thanks, Andy.
Cheers.

summary.overview: In the Business Development / M&A Consultation meeting between Manu of Nuva Digital and Andy from Capital A, key discussions revolved around the potential sale of Manu's e-commerce marketing agency, which has achieved a monthly revenue of approximately 100K AUD and a gross profit margin of 50%. Capital A, an M&A advisory firm, outlined their roll-up strategy and indicated that while Manu's agency, with a projected valuation of about 2.4M AUD, is currently below their threshold for acquisition, they can still connect him with potential buyers among their extensive network of 130,000 agencies. Manu shared his vision of franchising the business, and while the timeline for a potential exit is flexible, he is eager to explore options. Andy will follow up with a detailed seller package and engagement letter for Manu's review, as well as the necessary steps should he decide to proceed with the listing.
summary.short_summary: Manu, the founder of Nuva Digital, an e-commerce marketing agency in Sydney, met with Andy from Capital A, an M&A advisory firm, to discuss the potential sale of his business. With a monthly revenue of approximately 100K AUD and a gross profit margin of 50%, Manu's agency has a projected valuation of about 2.4M AUD. Although this is below Capital A's acquisition threshold, Andy offered to connect Manu with potential buyers from their network of 130,000 agencies. Manu shared his vision of franchising the business, with a flexible timeline for an exit strategy. Andy explained the acquisition process, including listing fees and commission structures, and highlighted the optimal timing for selling to American buyers before Thanksgiving. He will follow up with a detailed seller package for Manu's review.
